scope: Transactional file-effect confirmation separated from workspace and test validation

regression_proof.large_unrelated_artifact: A sparse 17 MiB opcode file exceeds the unchanged workspace digest limit. Actual write/edit/patch tools and finish_task still verify and finish the affected files when no checks are required/configured.
regression_proof.effects: Installed contents are compared before transaction observers; final hashes and absence of deleted files are checked again. Tool permissions, source-read requirements and rollback remain in place.
regression_proof.tampering: Same-size changes with restored mtime fail affected-file completion. Deletion/reappearance and symlink substitutions are rejected.
regression_proof.tests: File receipts never become test receipts. Configured/contract checks still require real, current-revision command receipts. Unavailable workspace/check verification preserves confirmed file effects with partial status.
regression_proof.commands: Terminal commands, hooks and opaque integrations retain complete workspace verification. A prior scoped write cannot bypass a failed command/workspace check.
regression_proof.persistence: Only paths and before/after hashes are stored in the existing workflow JSON; SQLite restart and resume preserve them, while a new independent turn clears them. Creation followed by deletion gives no net-change proof.
regression_proof.bounds: 128 affected paths per active scope, 16 MiB per final affected-file fingerprint, existing global limits unchanged; malformed and overflowing receipts fail atomically.
